note: Microsoft Learn's 'Impact analysis' article (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/governance/impact-analysis, last updated 05/23/2023 per the page itself, confirmed live and current via direct navigation on 2026-10-05) is a short, screenshot-dense page covering exactly this lesson's scope: what impact analysis assesses, the two entry points (lineage-view card icon, and the item details page's Lineage dropdown), how to read the pane (Child Items vs. All downstream items tabs, Browse by item type vs. Browse by workspace groupings, the data-source direct-children-only limitation, the connection-string detail for data sources), the Notify contacts flow, and the write-permission / 'Limited access' privacy rules. This lesson deliberately differentiates from Lesson 19 (Lineage in Fabric, same chapter): that lesson covers the lineage diagram itself; this lesson covers using impact analysis — a distinct, separate Fabric feature reachable from an item or from its lineage-view card — to quantify the downstream blast radius of a specific planned change before making it. All four of the article's screenshots were used, exceeding the 3-screenshot floor since this topic was flagged as one of the strongest screenshot candidates in the course.
